page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16 GB of system memory, providing 4 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core test scoring 1617.89 and Geekbench single-core reaching 1714.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3812.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3323.04. Memory bandwidth is also positioned in the lower tier, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 29.2 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform moderately well, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving 26.36 GB/sec and Passmark CPU encryption testing landing in the average range.

The inclusion of a dedicated 402 GB local NVMe SSD provides a storage-dense profile for a 4-vCPU instance, enhancing its qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring fast local scratch space. However, the trade-off lies in its limited multi-core scaling and lower memory bandwidth, which constrains its utility for memory-intensive or highly parallel computing. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, light database operations, and single-threaded processing tasks that benefit from fast local storage.
